app = binding.get("app_name", "Markor")
device.open_app(app)
device.settle(2)
if device.find(text="Markor") is None and \
   device.find(description="Create a new file or folder") is None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"App '{app}' did not open: Markor main screen not detected")

action.text: The squeaky wheel gets the grease.

steps.analysis: The action only depends on the note-content EditText (the editable, clickable text field) on Markor's editor screen; the recorded index 8 is unstable because the soft keyboard and IME elements shift indexes between instances. It can fail if no editable EditText exists yet, or if several exist (e.g., a filename field), so we look it up by class/editability and prefer the empty one (a new note).
steps.snippet:
els = device.elements()
candidates = [i for i, el in enumerate(els)
              if el.get('class_name') == 'EditText' and el.get('editable')]
if not candidates:
    raise RuntimeError("Markor note editor EditText not found on screen")
# Prefer the empty editor (new note) over any other editable field (e.g. filename)
idx = next((i for i in candidates if not els[i].get('text')), candidates[0])
device.click(idx)
device.input_text(binding['text'], index=idx)

steps.analysis: The recorded action is a global BACK press that dismisses the soft keyboard after typing the note text; it depends on nothing element-specific, so it only fails if the keyboard was never open or the back press would otherwise exit the editor. We keep it a plain global back with no lookup.
steps.snippet:
# Recorded action was a global navigate_back (no element addressed):
# dismisses the soft keyboard after entering note text.
before = device.elements()
device.navigate_back()
device.settle(1.0)
# Guard: ensure we are still in the editor (back should only close the keyboard)
after = device.elements()
if not after:
    raise RuntimeError("Unexpected state after navigate_back: no elements found (editor may have closed)")

steps.analysis: The navigate_back exits the editor (auto-saving) to the file list; it doesn't depend on element indexes, but it only makes sense if the editor with the target content was actually open — if back lands elsewhere or a save dialog appears, the flow fails.
steps.snippet:
# Leave the editor (text is auto-saved on back) and return to the file list
edit = device.find(editable=True)
if edit is None:
    raise RuntimeError("Editor with note text not open; cannot navigate back safely")
device.navigate_back()
device.settle(1.0)
if device.find(description="Create a new file or folder") is None:
    raise RuntimeError("Did not return to Markor main file list after back")

steps.analysis: The action long-presses the file list item for the target note, identified by its description starting with "File " plus the file name; on other screens indexes differ and the description prefix could be "File " or the item may need scrolling into view.

This action has no element dependency at all — it is a pure global back navigation, so differing element indexes cannot break it. On another instance it may dismiss the keyboard, close the editor back to MainActivity, or (as recorded) hit Markor's "Press 'Back' again to exit" guard at MainActivity; all are expected, and the note is already saved, so a single back is the faithful, robust rewrite. It could only fail if a modal dialog intercepted back, which this task family does not produce.
steps.snippet:
# Global action: no element lookup needed, indexes are irrelevant here.
device.navigate_back()
device.settle(1)
# Expected outcomes on any instance of the family: keyboard dismissed,
# editor popped to MainActivity, or Markor's "Press 'Back' again to exit"
# guard appears (harmless — the note is already saved).
